  "text": "At the top of the steps, Mara reached into her pocket for the photograph. Her fingers found only the torn lining.

The harbor master held his lantern toward her. “What is it?”

She shook her head. Below them, the gate gave a single metallic knock. The tide was coming in.

They crossed the empty square together. At the corner, the woman took Mara’s hand, as she had when Mara was small and frightened of the bell. Mara almost pulled away. Instead, she asked, “Which one did you find on the quay?”

The woman stopped. For a moment Mara heard nothing but water running through the gutters.

“You,” she said at last. “I thought it was you.”

In the pocket of Mara’s coat, something shifted. She drew out a shell, pale and wet, no bigger than her palm. Its edge had been chipped in the same place as the one in the passage.

The man from the boat stepped back. The woman released Mara’s hand.

Mara held the shell to her ear. She expected the sea, or the child’s voice. Instead she heard the bell above the quay, ringing once. Beneath it came the sound of her own footsteps, quick and uneven, climbing the steps.

She lowered the shell. Across the square, a little girl in a damp coat stood under the streetlamp. She looked exactly as Mara had in the photograph.

The girl glanced toward the harbor, then raised one hand to wave. Mara raised hers in return. By the time the bell rang again, the streetlamp illuminated only rain."
